class.name: FauxStructuralSource
class.brief_description: Production real-content entry point: mounts a GRP or loose directory, reads a MAP through the VFS, derives the structural world, and presents it to a [FauxBuildView].

description.para: [b]Source-side operation only, never rendering.[/b] This class owns the one legitimate GDScript-facing real-content route: core mount (GRP archive or loose directory) → VFS lookup of the MAP name → core MAP reader → core structural derivation → [code]StructuralWorld[/code] → the view's C++ presentation seam. The view stays a pure consumer; generated meshes stay disposable presentation.

Failure is transactional: a load that fails anywhere returns [code]false[/code], records a stage-tagged structured error in [method get_last_error], leaves the previously presented world untouched, and does not update the reporting facts — they keep describing the last successful load. MapData is never retained or exposed as script-authoritative state.
Mounts the GRP archive at [param grp_path] in place (no extraction) and presents the MAP found under the VFS name [param map_name] to [param view].
Mounts the loose directory at [param dir_path] and presents the MAP found under the (case-insensitively matched) VFS name [param map_name] to [param view].
Mount description of the last successful load, e.g. [code]grp:/path/to/archive.grp[/code].
Normalized VFS name that was read by the last successful load.
Sector count of the last successfully loaded map (reporting only).
Wall count of the last successfully loaded map (reporting only).
Structural surface count of the last successful derivation (reporting only).
Triangle count of the last successful derivation (reporting only).
Deferral-note count of the last successful derivation (reporting only).
Nonfatal diagnostic count of the last successful derivation (reporting only).

The map's own parsed start position for the last successful load, converted through the single core transform ([code]to_render_space[/code]) like every other coordinate — never a second transform. Diagnostic state only, never authority: the human viewer uses it to aim its overview and to place its start-position camera. The start ANGLE is deliberately not exposed; Build angle semantics are not M5's.
